variable.plain_summary: Not a planet, but still interesting: this star changes brightness on its own; its brightness changes every 2.9 days as dark spots on its surface turn in and out of view.
key_facts: Starspots, like sunspots, make one side darker; as the star spins its brightness rises and falls.
Time for one full cycle of brightening and fading.
How much the brightness varies (5th to 95th percentile).
How much of the brightness change one regular cycle explains. Near 1: very regular (pulsation); low: irregular (spots that come and go).
How much the period differs from one observing sector to the next.

Strength of the second harmonic relative to the first: 0 for a smooth wave, larger for sharp, lopsided cycles such as pulsating stars. Values above 1 usually mean the period found is a multiple of the true one, so they are not shown.
